title: Signal · Monday 9 November
overview: Nvidia's board opens an investigation after reports its chief executive was targeted by foreign intelligence, Anthropic's IPO talk falls to about USD 1.2 trillion as OpenAI raises at USD 1.25 trillion, and South Korea moves to scrap bank network separation rules after AI-assisted hacks.

top.headline: Nvidia's board opens independent investigation after reports its CEO was targeted by foreign intelligence
top.summary: Nvidia's board said on 8 November that a committee of independent directors, with outside counsel, will investigate reporting that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. It said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and that it has confidence in Huang, who told staff in a memo Nvidia published that he had been unfaithful to his wife.
top.background: NBC News said The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that a woman he had a relationship with, whose Singapore company bought Nvidia's advanced chips, had been recruited by Chinese intelligence; a person familiar with the matter told NBC that US agencies had reached that view.
top.why: Nvidia sits at the centre of AI chip supply and US export policy, so a governance question over its founder reaches every portfolio and budget that leans on the AI trade.
top.watch_next: Nvidia reports third-quarter results on 17 November.

top.headline: Update: AI lab valuations reset as Anthropic IPO talk falls to USD 1.2 trillion
top.summary: Prospective buyers of Anthropic's IPO are discussing a valuation of USD 1.2 trillion to USD 1.3 trillion, some as low as USD 1.1 trillion, according to Bloomberg as cited by Yahoo Finance, against as much as USD 2 trillion projected in early October. OpenAI has raised USD 11 billion at a USD 1.25 trillion valuation, in a round expected to reach about USD 20 billion against a USD 30 billion target, TechCrunch reported, citing Bloomberg.
top.background: The Nasdaq Composite had its worst daily decline since April 2025 on 5 November as investors weighed the midterm results and the AI data centre build-out, Yahoo Finance reported. Odds on prediction markets of an Anthropic listing before 1 December fell from roughly 80 to near 50 percent.
top.why: A drop of more than a third in a month resets expectations for the whole AI supply chain, and shows that vendor economics behind multi-year bank AI contracts remain unsettled.
top.watch_next: Whether Anthropic keeps its expected pre-Thanksgiving listing, and at what valuation.

top.headline: South Korea will phase out bank network separation rules after AI-assisted hacks
top.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission said on 5 November it will phase out the rules requiring financial firms to keep internal networks separate from the internet, with a task force drafting an AI-based replacement by the first quarter of 2027. It reported 40 breaches at 37 firms between 30 September and 3 November, exposing more than 473,000 records.
top.background: The rules date from 2013, after a cyberattack paralysed banks and broadcasters. Firms say they block access to cloud and AI security tools; better-prepared firms will move first, and experts warn against lifting protections before alternatives are ready.
top.why: A supervisor has concluded that isolating bank networks no longer suffices against AI-assisted attacks, a question boards and CISOs at Swiss and European banks can expect to be asked.
top.watch_next: The commission's plan in early 2027, and its year-end review of 580 financial firms.

items.headline: Swiss digital health platform dacadoo in liquidation; Israel's movement buys its assets
items.summary: Israel-based wellness group movement has acquired the technology and intellectual property of Swiss digital health company dacadoo, whose platform is used by insurers, health organisations and employers in dozens of countries. The Swiss company dacadoo ag is now in liquidation, according to a press release carried by Startupticker on 6 November; customers can keep using the platform.
items.why: Insurers using dacadoo should confirm continuity and data arrangements with the new owner now that the Swiss company is being wound up.

items.headline: Progressive Building Society replaces 20-year-old treasury system, reaching parallel run in ten days
items.summary: Progressive Building Society has replaced the treasury system it used for more than 20 years with Cobalt from ALMIS International, FinTech Global reported on 6 November, going from contract to parallel run in 10 days. Cobalt puts front, middle and back-office treasury on one system with a single data source.
items.why: A reported ten days from contract to parallel run will set expectations among smaller lenders weighing treasury replacements, though the figure comes from the vendor's announcement.

items.headline: NH NongHyup Bank presents ten AI work agents built with its own AI subsidiary
items.summary: NH NongHyup Bank presented 10 AI work agents built with its subsidiary AgileSoDA, Seoul Economic Daily reported on 6 November. For project finance reviews, the agents read 500 to 1,000 pages and pull 318 items into a draft report; the bank expects drafting that took at least five business days to fall to about four hours.
items.why: Document-heavy credit reviews are where banks can show hard time savings first, and choosing 10 agents from 39 staff proposals is a usable prioritisation model.

items.headline: Banque Heritage CEO rejects sale rumours and plans an external asset management arm
items.summary: Chief executive Marcos Esteve told finews on 9 November that selling the Geneva bank is not part of its strategy and that it is evaluating a move into external asset management as a second pillar. He targets CHF 20 billion in assets, about 15 percent growth a year, and has more than 20 professionals in Zurich.
items.why: A family-owned bank building a platform for external managers tests whether custody synergies can win independents already being courted by consolidators.

items.headline: Mediobanca's nine-month profit rises 13.3 percent while wealth profit falls 21.7 percent
items.summary: Mediobanca reported attributable net profit of EUR 1.09 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up 13.3 percent, with a CET1 ratio of 15.0 percent, WealthBriefing reported on 6 November. Wealth management profit fell 21.7 percent to EUR 164.9 million on a higher tax rate and EUR 28 million of one-off charges.
items.why: Now fully controlled by another bank and being delisted, Mediobanca shows how a wealth franchise performs inside a domestic takeover.

items.headline: US banks brace for tighter oversight after Democrats win both houses of Congress
items.summary: Large US banks expect closer scrutiny once Democrats take control of Congress in January, Reuters reported via cash.ch on 7 November, with fees, credit terms and mortgages in focus. Elizabeth Warren is favoured to chair the Senate Banking Committee and Maxine Waters the House Financial Services Committee. Banks plan to press technology firms on fraud.
items.why: Deregulatory gains of the past two years face new pressure, and banks with US operations, UBS among them, will plan for hearings.

items.headline: Paraguay's president resigns as digital lender ueno's collapse becomes a state crisis
items.summary: Paraguay's central bank ordered the resolution of ueno bank on 2 November after it breached solvency rules, freezing deposits of about three million customers, finews reported on 6 November. Authorities are guaranteeing deposits. President Santiago Peña, who says he sold his shares in the controlling Grupo Vázquez in March 2025, resigned on 5 November amid allegations he denies.
items.why: A neobank holding about USD 850 million of state money failed amid alleged related-party lending, a case study in ownership risk behind fast-growing digital banks.

items.headline: DeepMind says AI agents found two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA
items.summary: Google DeepMind said on 6 November that AI agents, guided by human cryptanalysts, found a signature forgery attack on legacy 1024-bit RSA and a way to factor many keys at once about 30 times more cheaply than the best prior batch method, a theoretical estimate. It says 2048-bit keys are not threatened.
items.why: 1024-bit keys survive in old hardware and long-lived certificates, so banks should check inventories now, as AI shortens the time such analysis takes.

items.headline: Ramp data shows AI spending flat over late summer despite rising token volumes
items.summary: Token spend grew 1.5 percent across August and September, against 42 percent in July, according to Ramp data cited by TechCrunch on 6 November, before rising 8.9 percent between 23 September and 23 October. Ramp's economist points to price competition; Anthropic said price cuts reduced its revenue growth by about USD 600 million.
items.why: Enterprise buyers have room to negotiate now, and AI budget lines should not assume spending or prices move in a straight line.

items.headline: Researchers find more than 800 exposed deployments of the Artex AI hacking tool
items.summary: Censys found more than 800 deployments of Artex, an open-source autonomous penetration testing tool made in China, reachable from the web without a password, TechCrunch reported on 6 November. Artex has been linked to attacks including on the Korean finance industry; attack data on one exposed instance extended well beyond South Korean banks, Censys said.
items.why: Attacks using such tools mostly exploit weak passwords and missing multi-factor authentication, so basic access controls remain banks' first line of defence.

items.headline: Anthropic buys USD 3.4 billion in gas generators; Google takes over Crusoe's Wyoming project
items.summary: Anthropic has secured about 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions for around USD 3.4 billion including installation, the Financial Times reported, according to Reuters via cash.ch on 8 November. Separately, Crusoe confirmed selling an unfinished Wyoming data centre project to Google, which plans to invest USD 17 billion there, TechCrunch reported.
items.why: Power and construction now limit AI capacity as much as chips do, which feeds through to the cost and timing of enterprise capacity.

items.headline: Valais rolls out AVA, an in-house sovereign AI platform built on open models
items.summary: The canton of Valais has made AVA available to its whole administration after a six-month build, ICTjournal reported on 6 November. It runs open models including Apertus, Mistral and Qwen on dedicated GPUs in Switzerland, served more than 2,000 staff in pilot and costs CHF 2 per daily active user a month by the canton's estimate.
items.why: A public Swiss reference for running open models in-house: banks weighing sovereign deployment can compare cost and architecture, which the canton plans to open-source.

items.headline: Update: FINMA tells intermediaries to apply sanctions, including a ban on Russian crypto ownership
EBA extends supervisory reporting timelines to December 2027, some areas to December 2028
ECB data: EU banks' CET1 16.43 percent, non-performing loans 1.99 percent at end-June
Partners Group hires three for European infrastructure, including CPP's former data centre strategy lead
Basel-Stadt adopts a 2026 to 2029 AI strategy with 21 goals for its administration

this_week.event: BAK and the Association of Foreign Banks launch a foreign banks barometer
Swiss Finance Institute annual meeting on the impact of AI on finance, Zurich

say_it_today: South Korea is dismantling the network separation rules it introduced in 2013 because attackers now use AI and defenders need tools that isolated networks cannot reach, which is a fair question for any bank's next security review.
